profiles.name: Michael B. First
profiles.heading: Across disciplines, with a mentor
profiles.narrative: Michael B. First's Columbia biography follows a route from electrical engineering and computer science into medicine and psychiatry. It names Robert Spitzer as his mentor during a biometrics research fellowship. That path gives context to the biography's description of his work on diagnostic questions and structured assessment tools, alongside a Manhattan practice.

profiles.name: Jamielynn Hanam-Jahr
profiles.heading: From intensive care to dentistry
profiles.narrative: Jamielynn Hanam-Jahr's practice biography begins her career story in a steel town outside Pittsburgh, before nursing work in surgical and trauma intensive care. It traces her move into dentistry through New Orleans and later California. The same account describes Give Back A Smile volunteer work, and interests in cooking, music, piano, learning guitar and photography. These are the practice's descriptions of her journey and life outside work, not independently checked credentials or a promise about care.

profiles.name: Tasheka Cox
profiles.sourceTitle: Meet Dr. Cox — My Philosophy and A Little About My Story
profiles.heading: The experience behind her approach
profiles.narrative: On her named biography, Tasheka Cox connects her professional work with her own experience of learning to understand the protective patterns behind achievement and independence. She describes this realization as a foundation of her professional work. Her stated approach asks what a pattern once protected and focuses on noticing it before intentionally choosing a response. This is Cox's account of her motivation and approach, not evidence that therapy will produce a particular outcome.

claimMap.claim: On her named biography, Tasheka Cox connects her professional work with her own experience of learning to understand the protective patterns behind achievement and independence.
claimMap.excerpt: The more I achieved, the more I felt secure. Independence helped me feel protected. [...] My healing journey taught me that I did not need to reject the high achieving woman I had become. I needed to understand her

claimMap.claim: She describes this realization as a foundation of her professional work.
claimMap.excerpt: That realization became deeply personal and eventually, it became the foundation of my professional work.

claimMap.claim: Her stated approach asks what a pattern once protected and focuses on noticing it before intentionally choosing a response.
claimMap.excerpt: exploring the protective purpose beneath the pattern [...] we want to notice when they are present and intentionally choose how to respond instead of automatically reacting.
